response: Yes, failures of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction have been associated with steep posterior tibial slopes. Studies have shown that a steeper posterior tibial slope can increase the risk of ACL graft failure, as it can lead to increased stress and strain on the graft. This is because a steep posterior tibial slope can cause the tibia to slope backward, which can put additional tension on the ACL graft and increase the risk of it failing.
